# Jubilees Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abraham's Youth; Idolatry of Ur; Early Righteousness

---

**11:1** And in the thirty-fifth jubilee, in the third week, in the first year thereof, Reu took to himself a wife, and her name was 'Ora, the daughter of 'Ur, the son of Kesed; and she bore him a son, and he called his name Sarugh, in the seventh year of this week.

**11:2** And the sons of Noah began to war on each other, to take captive and to slay each other, and to shed the blood of men on the earth, and to eat blood, and to build strong cities, and walls, and towers, and individuals (began) to exalt themselves above the nation, and to found the beginnings of kingdoms, and to go to war people against people, and nation against nation, and city against city, and all (began) to do evil, and to acquire arms, and to teach their sons war, and they began to capture cities, and to sell male and female slaves.

**11:3** And Mastema sent ravens and birds to devour the seed which was sown in the land, in order to destroy the land, and to rob the children of men of their labors. Before they could plow in the seed, the ravens picked it from the surface of the ground.

**11:4** And for this reason he called that name Reu; for evil was the time, and they were devouring one another.

**11:5** And Sarugh took to himself a wife, and her name was Melka, the daughter of Kaber, the daughter of his father's brother, in the thirty-sixth jubilee, in the fifth week, in the first year thereof.

**11:6** And she bore him Nahor, in the first year of the third week. And he grew and dwelt in Ur of the Chaldees, and his father taught him the researches of the Chaldees to divine and to augur, according to the signs of heaven.

**11:7** And in the thirty-seventh jubilee in the sixth week, in the first year thereof, he took to himself a wife, and her name was 'Ijaska, the daughter of Nestag of the Chaldees.

**11:8** And she bore him Terah in the seventh year of this week.

**11:9** And the prince Mastema sent ravens and birds to devour the seed before it was plowed in, and they were destroying all the work of the children of men, and he sent a destroying angel among them.

**11:10** And in the thirty-ninth jubilee, in the second week in the first year, Terah took to himself a wife, and her name was 'Edna', the daughter of 'Abram, the daughter of his father's brother.

**11:11** And she bore him a son in the seventh year of this week, and he called his name Abram, after the name of the father of his mother; for he had died before his daughter had borne a son.

**11:12** And the child began to understand the errors of the earth that all went astray after graven images and after uncleanness, and his father taught him writing.

**11:13** And he sought and understood the judgment of God, and set himself apart from his father, and he would not worship idols with his father.

**11:14** And he prayed to God that he would have mercy on him and rescue him from the errors of the children of men, and that his portion should not fall in the error of uncleanness and the abomination of idol-worship.

**11:15** And the days were coming on when there was sowing time, and they all went out together to protect their seed against the ravens, for in those days, all the ravens and kites devoured the seed which was sown.

**11:16** And Abram went out in the morning to protect the seed, and a cloud of ravens came to eat the seed.

**11:17** And Abram ran to meet them before they settled on the ground, and he cried to them and said: "Descend not: return to the place whence ye came!" And they returned.

**11:18** And on that day seventy times did he drive them back, and not a single one settled on any of the fields of his father.

**11:19** And he remembered this day and wrote it down as a memorial.

**11:20** And as the sun was setting his father called him, and he made him sit with him, and he said unto him: "O my son, what wonderful things hast thou done this day, and how truly thou art born to be mine!"

**11:21** And Abram told his father everything, and said: "Because of the devastation of the ravens to the whole land I protected our seed."

**11:22** And his father rejoiced exceedingly, and Abram was great before his father.

**11:23** And Terah his father said unto him: "Thus will it be with thy seed all thy days; the ravens will devour it not."

**11:24** And in the sixtieth year of the life of Abram, that is, in the fourth week, in the fourth year thereof, Abram arose by night, and burned the house of the idols, and he burned everything in the house.

**11:25** And he burned all that was in the house, and no man knew it; and they arose in the night and sought to save their gods from the midst of the fire.

**11:26** And Haran hastened to save them, but the fire flamed over him, and he was burnt in the fire, and he died in Ur of the Chaldees before Terah his father, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldees.

**11:27** And Terah went forth from Ur of the Chaldees, he and his sons, to go into the land of Lebanon and into the land of Canaan, and he dwelt in the land of Haran, and Abram dwelt with his father in Haran two weeks of years.

---
*EMET notes: Mastema's agricultural sabotage (vv.3,9) = demonic activity in the world after the flood. Abram's bird-chasing episode (vv.16-19) — not in Genesis — shows his pre-call righteousness. Haran's death in the idol-fire (v.26) is a Jubilees-unique tradition (cf. rabbinic tradition in Gen. Rabbah 38). "Sixtieth year" (v.24) = jubilee chronology.*
